operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9675 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

Washington, Tuesday, January 8, 1946
The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9674 
Liquidation  op W ar A gencies
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and statutes, includ­
ing Title I of the First War Powers Act, 
1941 (55 Stat. 838), and as President of 
the United States, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
1. There shall be in the Office for 
Emergency Management of the Execu­
tive Office of the President a Director of 
Liquidation, hereinafter referred to as 
the Director, who shall be appointed by 
the President and who shall perform his 
functions in consultation with a Liqui­
dation Advisory Committee.
The Liquidation Advisory Committee 
shall be composed of one representative 
of each of the following agencies: the 
Department of the Treasury, the Sur­
plus Property Administration, the Na­
tional Archives, the Civil Service Com­
mission, the Public Buildings Adminis­
tration, the General Accounting Office, 
and the Bureau of the Budget. The 
chairman of the Committee shall be 
designated by the Director from the 
Committee’ s membership.
2. It shall be the duty of the Director 
to further proper preparations, arrange­
ments, and methods for the orderly and 
timely winding up of the affairs of the 
temporary Federal agencies created for 
the purposes of the war, hereinafter re­
ferred to as war agencies, particularly 
with respect to personnel, property, ac­
counts, space, and records. To this end 
the Director shall:
(a) Cause to be developed by each war 
agency, for use whenever it shall, pur­
suant to Act of Congress or order of the 
President, as the case may be, cease the 
performance of its substantive functions 
or . materially reduce the volume of its 
activities, suitable plans for the winding 
up or retrenchment of its affairs.
(b) When deemed appropriate, ar­
range for the designation, by the head 
of any war agency, of a liquidation of­
ficer for the agency.
(c) Receive periodic reports which 
.be submitted by each war agency,
showing the status of preparation for 
liquidation, or of liquidation, as the case may be.
(d) Establish such uniform liquida­
tion practices as will accelerate the rate 
or improve the quality of the liquidation.
(e) Suggest to the Civil Service Com­
mission and the Liaison Officer for Per­
sonnel Management measures designed 
to ameliorate the impact of liquidation 
upon the employees of the war agencies 
liquidated.
(f) Advise and assist the war agencies 
in such other respects as will facilitate 
the preparation for and the carrying 
out of the liquidation of their affairs.
3. Nothing in this order shall be 
deemed to divest any agency referred to 
in paragraph 1 of this order of any of 
its functions which may be concerned 
with the liquidation of a war agency. 
The functions of the Director shall not 
be deemed to extend to the affairs of 
any agency which has heretofore been, 
or shall hereafter be, abolished and the 
affairs of which are transferred to the 
Department of the Treasury, or to any 
other department, for the final winding 
up of such affairs. -
4. The Director may, within the limits 
of funds which may be made available, 
employ personnel and make provisions 
for supplies, facilities, and services, and 
incur other expenses, necessary to dis­
charge the functions of the Director un­
der this order.
Harry S. T ruman
The W hite  H ouse,
January 4, 1946.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9675 at 11 FR 333 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed January 5, 1946; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the January 8, 1946 issue. Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 15862 to 16749 of the held text, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence; the dossier span includes unrelated Federal Register page text. The order's heading and recitals precede it in the held text and contain no command. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the St. Louis-San Francisco Railway Company and the St. Louis, San Francisco and Texas Railway Company, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the St. Louis-San Francisco Railway Company and the St. Louis, San Francisco and Texas Railway Company or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9675 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate said dispute. No member 
of the said board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any-organization 
of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Hudson &  Manhattan Railroad Com­
pany, a carrier, and certain of its em­
ployees represented by the Brotherhood 
of Locomotive Engineers and the Broth­
erhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor or­
ganizations; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the states of 
New York and New Jersey, to a degree 
such as to deprive that portion of the 
country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U.S.C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate said dispute. No member 
of the said board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any-organization 
of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9731 at 11 FR 5893 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed May 29, 1946; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the June 1, 1946 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3523 to 4015 and 16948 to 17272 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Hudson & Manhattan Railroad Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Hudson & Manhattan Railroad Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9731 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to nvestigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing and in the printing of Executive Order 9730, on whose Federal Register page this order's heading also appears; none of those texts acts on this order. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25. The dossier's machine lead naming Executive Order 9730 is a Federal Register page on which the heading Executive Order 9731 stands above an amendment of Executive Order No. 9630; that is a different instrument, unrelated to this board, and is not a later event of this order.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

The bounded search covered the held text of Executive Order 12553, the order's own text and the OFR catalog disposition notes.

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said disputes.
Each of the carriers involved shall be 
given independent consideration in such 
investigation, and the said labor organ­
izations shall be permitted to function 
as a unit in proceedings before the 
board.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9793 at 11 FR 12695 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed October 25, 1946; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the October 29, 1946 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3633 to 4069 and 15895 to 16332 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between The Atlanta & St. Andrews Bay Railway Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the fifteen cooperating railway labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; directs that each carrier involved be given independent consideration and that the labor organizations be permitted to function as a unit in proceedings before the board; requires the board's report to contain separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Lists A and B (the carriers and the labor organizations) follow the signature block in the held text; they identify the parties and are not separate commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9793 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to nvestigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill and the further commands noted in the inventory all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9855 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

Tuesday ,  May 20 , 1947 FEDERAL REGISTER 3241
§ 300.17 Delegation of authority to  
State Director of the Farmers Home Ad­
ministration for Washington and Ore­
gon to sell certain lands in Jefferson  
County, Oregon.  Pursuant to the au­
thority vested in the Administrator of 
the Farmers Home Administration by 
the Acting Secretary’s Delegation of Au- \  
thority issued May 2, 1947 (12 F. R. 
3047), covering certain therein described 
lands located in Jefferson County, Ore­
gon, and pursuant to the Order of the 
Secretary issued October 14, 1946 (11 
F. R. 12520), It is hereby ordered,  That:
(a) Subject to the provisions of this 
section all of the functions, powers, du­
ties, and responsibilities conferred upon 
the Administrator of the Farmers Home 
Administration with respect to said 
lands and loans for the acquisition and 
improvement thereof shall be exercised 
and performed by the State Director of 
the Farmers Home Administration for 
the States of Washington and Oregon. 
In exercise of this authority the State 
Director shall:
(1) Determine, after certification 
thereof by the County Committee, which 
of the lands among those described in 
the aforesaid delegation of authority 
by the Secretary are suitable for sale 
to individual purchasers in furtherance 
of the purposes of Title 1  of the Bank- 
head-Jones Farm Tenant Act, as 
amended.
(2) Subdivide suitable lands into eco­
nomic family-type farm-management 
units, which shall have a value, as im­
proved, of not in excess of $13,000, none 
ot which shall contain in excess of 160 
acres of irrigable land, with boundaries 
conforming as nearly as may be practi­
cable to General Land Office survey 
boundaries.
(3) Select applicants to purchase said 
farms in accordance, with existing au­
thority and procedures under Title 1  of 
the Bankhead-Jones Farm Tenant Act, 
as amended.
(4) Sell said farms to approved ap­
plicants at prices based upon the earn­
ing capacity values of the farm units, 
taking into consideration the improve­
ments necessary to make the farm an 
economic family-type farm and reim­
bursable construction and water charges 
and other fixed charges against the land.
(5) Execute conveyances of said land 
on behalf of the United States which 
shall recite his determination of suitabil­
ity of the land as required in this section; 
shall reserve all of the interest of the 
United States in the fissionable materials 
and at least three-fourths of the interest 
of the United States in all other minerals 
in or under said lands, provided that all 
such interests shall be reserved if* the 
State Director finds that minerals or 
mineral rights in the area have a com­
mercial value; and shall preserve the 
lien of the United States for reclamation 
and irrigation charges.
(6) Make loans for the purchase price 
and for the costs of the improvement of 
farm'units sold under this section and 
take and service security therefor, in 
accordance with the applicable provi­
sions of the Bankhead-Jones Farm Ten­
ant Act, as amended, and existing pro­
cedures and instructions of the Farmers 
Home Administration as nearly as pos­
sible, except that:
(i) An option to purchase will not be 
executed.
(ii) Loan approval will be by the State 
Director.
(iii) The loan and the borrower’sjntal 
investment in his farm may exceed the 
county loan limit but shall not exceed 
the average value of efficient family- 
type farm-management units located in 
Jefferson County, Oregon, as determined 
by the Secretary of Agriculture (11 F. R. 
13611).
(iv) Title insurance will not be re­
quired. Title clearance will be effected 
in accordance with requirements of the 
representative of the Office of the Solici­
tor and will include a judgment and lien 
search against the prospective purchaser 
and procurement of an abstract continu­
ation through a date showing conveyance 
of the property to the applicant and 
execution of the Mortgage in favor of the 
United States. The cost of title clear­
ance shall be paid by the applicant.
*  (b) The functions, powers, and duties 
authorized in this section may be per­
formed and exercised by the Acting State 
Director during the absence of the State 
Director.
(c) The provisions of this section shall 
take effect immediately and shall remain 
in effect until revoked or superseded by 
order of the Administrator. (Acting Sec­
retary’ «  delegation of authority, May 2, 
1947, 12 F. R. 3047; Secretary’s order, 
Oct. 14, 1946, 11 F. R. 12520)
Issued this 14th day of May 1947.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9855 at 12 FR 3239 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed May 16, 1947; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the May 20, 1947 issue. Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 2301 to 3124 of the held text, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence; the dossier's sixteen clause spans (the first beginning at the order's heading) run on through unrelated Federal Register regulation text in the same issue and do not follow the order's own paragraphs. The order's heading and recitals precede it in the held text and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Bingham & Garfield Railway Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen and the Order of Railway Conductors of America, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Bingham & Garfield Railway Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9855 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

The bounded search covered the held text of Executive Order 12553, the order's own text and the OFR catalog disposition notes.

The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). WHEREAS the Departments of the 
Army and the Air Force are engaged in 
public-work activities which are essen­

lishment and fulfilment of international 
commitments of the United States; and 
WHEREAS employees of the Depart­

upon other portions of which employees 
of contractors are working in excess of 
eight hours a day ; and 
WHEREAS such employees of the De­
partments of the Army and the Air Forcé 
are not able by working only eight hours 
a day to carry on the Government work 
at the same rate as the contract work, 
and the completion of such projects is 
thereby frequently delayed; and 
WHEREAS by section 1  of the act of 
August 1,1892 (27 Stat. 340), as amended 
by the act-of March 3,1913 (37 Stat. 726, 
40 U. S. C. 321), the services of laborers 
and mechanics employed by the Govern­
ment of the United States upon any pub­
lic work of the United States is limited 
to eight hours in any one calendar day, 
except in case of extraordinary emer­
gency; and
WHEREAS I find that *  as to those 
activities essential to the support of.the 
military forces or urgent construction 
projects being performed by or for the 
Departments of the Army and the Air 
Force an extraordinary emergency 
exists *
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 1  of the 
said act of August 1,1892, as amended by 
the said act of March 3, 1913, and as 
President of the United States, I hereby 
suspend until July 1, 1948, the above- 
mentioned provisions of law, prohibiting 
more than eight hours of labor in any 
one day by laborers and mechanics em­
ployed by the Government of the United 
States, as to all work performed by 
laborers and mechanics employed by the 
Department of the Army or the Depart­
ment of the Air Force with respect to 
which the Secretary of the Army or the
Secretary of the Air Force, respectively, 
shall find suspension essential to (1) the 
supply and maintenance I3f~the Army or 
the Air Force, (2) the completion of es­
sential construction, or (3) the fulfil­
ment of international commitments: 
Provided, That the wages of all laborers 
and mechanics so employed by the De­
partment of the Army or the Department 
of the Air Force shall lie computed on a 
basic day rate of eight hours of work 
with overtime to be paid at time and one- 
half for dll hours of work in excess of 
eight hours in any one day.
Executive Order No. 9290 of December 
28, 1942, entitled “Suspension of Eight- 
Hour Law as to Laborers and Mechanics 
Employed by the War Department on 
Public Works within the United States,” 
is hereby superseded.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9899 at 12 FR 6781 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed October 15, 1947; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the October 16, 1947 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 4457 to 4652 and 11556 to 12227 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span was replaced because the dossier's single span begins in the middle of a contents page of the issue. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Atlanta & West Point Rail Road Company and the Western Railway of Alabama, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Atlanta & West Point Rail Road Company and the Western Railway of Alabama or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9899 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to nvestigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing and in the printing of Executive Order 9898, on whose Federal Register page this order's heading also appears; none of those texts acts on this order. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9910 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to nvestigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9910 at 12 FR 8439 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed December 16, 1947; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the December 18, 1947 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 622 to 3694 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Georgia Railroad, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Georgia Railroad or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 9910 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to nvestigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9942 describes providing for performance of functions under the Rubber Act of 1948). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The order was amended once before its end: Executive Order 10539 of June 22, 1954 deleted "Reconstruction Finance Corporation" from sections 2 and 3 and inserted "Federal Facilities Corporation." in each place; the clause continued, as amended. No earlier end is shown in held evidence; the Rubber Act of 1948 is not held, and the order is claimed as ending on the revocation.

which a bank holds future payment

of stock and the future payment funds  
held in connection with a loan are suffi­
cient to pay off the loan in full, they may

tired for that purpose;
(c) When the amount of bank stock  
held as security for a loan is sufficient to  
complete payment of the loan, the bank  
may retire its stock and, with the con­
sent of the association, credit an amount  
equal to the par value thereof as a last  
payment on the retiring borrower’s loan;

due and payable for the purpose of ac­
cepting deed, the bank may retire the  
related stock and apply the proceeds to

lying security on the books of the bank;  
and

a land bank loan is transferred and the  
present owner thereof assumes the mort­
gage indebtedness, but either fails to ac­
quire ownership of the stock interest on

bership in the association endorsing the

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9942 at 13 FR 1823 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 1, 1948; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 3, 1948 issue. The register title is Providing for the Performance of Certain Functions Under the Rubber Act of 1948.  Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 734 to 2164 of the held text, from the authority recital through paragraph 4 and its effective date. The dossier splits the order into a lead clause, paragraphs 1 to 4 and a separate fragment holding only the year of the effective date ("1948."), which is not a command. Content: paragraph 1 has the Secretary of Commerce perform the functions the President holds under sections 3, 4, 18(c) and 18(d) of the Rubber Act of 1948; paragraph 2 has the Reconstruction Finance Corporation perform those under sections 5(c), 5(e), 6, 7, 8, 11(a) and 18(f), with a proviso about section 6(a); paragraph 3 divides the functions under sections 10 and 12 between them; paragraph 4 makes the order effective April 1, 1948. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9942 describes providing for performance of functions under the Rubber Act of 1948). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Later event: Executive Order 10539 of June 22, 1954 (held text, section 2) amends this order by deleting from sections 2 and 3 the words "Reconstruction Finance Corporation" and inserting in each case the words "Federal Facilities Corporation." Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments it is a later event, not an end; the order continued, as amended, until the revocation. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain no end date or termination clause; paragraph 4 sets the effective date. The dossier chain names Executive Order 10539 (amendment) and Executive Order 12553 (revocation). The Rubber Act of 1948 is not held in the packet, so whether the statute's own expiry or later rubber-facility disposal legislation ended these functions before 1986 cannot be checked, and no end is claimed on that ground. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: no fixed end date or termination clause appears in the order; paragraph 4 sets only an effective date; the dossier chain names no acting instrument other than Executive Orders 10539 and 12553; the Rubber Act of 1948 is not held, so any end by expiry of that statute cannot be tested and is not claimed.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 allocate functions under one statute between two officers and paragraph 4 sets the effective date; none has a separate sunset in its text, and the revocation is the first held instrument that ends any of them.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 has no saving clause; the order allocates functions between officers and creates no appointment, transfer or accrued right in any held source.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry describes its subject, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so the revocation reaches every paragraph."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause; the order only allocated statutory functions, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in the held text of the order, Executive Order 12553 or the OFR catalog notes.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9949 describes amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The order was amended once before its end: Executive Order 10415 of December 2, 1952 struck out "within five years from the date of his transfer to such Board" in the second paragraph and inserted "on or before December 31, 1953"; the clause continued, as amended. The time limit conditions the employee's right and is not shown to end the clause. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9949 at 13 FR 2089 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 17, 1948; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 20, 1948 issue. The register title is Modifying Executive Order No. 9721, Providing for the Transfer of Personnel to Certain Public International Organizations.  Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 1000 to 2347 of the held text, from the authority recital to the direction that the order be published in the Federal Register. It modifies paragraph 3(a) of Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946 for one named employee, Paul D. Miles, on transfer from the Federal Communications Commission to the International Frequency Registration Board of the International Telecommunication Union: he is to have the reemployment rights the parent order gives if his service with that Board is terminated without prejudice within five years of his transfer, in place of the three years the parent order requires, provided he complies with all other provisions of the parent order. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9949 describes amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Later event: Executive Order 10415 of December 2, 1952 (held text, enacting sentence) amends this order by striking out the words "within five years from the date of his transfer to such Board" in its second paragraph and inserting in their place the words "on or before December 31, 1953". It has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments it is a later event with before and after text, not an end; the modification continued, as amended, until the revocation. Earlier-end check: no end date or termination clause appears in the order; the five-year window, and the fixed date that replaced it, condition the employee's reemployment right and are not an end of the order; no held source shows when or whether the employee transferred. Executive Order 10804 of February 12, 1959 (held text, American Presidency Project transcription, section 2) revokes the parent Executive Order 9721 and Executive Order 10103, with an exception that each remains in effect for employees serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who do not elect coverage under that Act, and for rights and benefits vested before that date. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9965 at 13 FR 3009 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed June 3, 1948; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the June 5, 1948 issue. Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 12151 to 13200 of the held text, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence; the dossier's span begins in the middle of the enacting clause and so omits the order's opening words after the recitals. The order's heading and recitals precede it in the held text and contain no command. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the National Airlines, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, International, and the International Association of Machinists, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members whom it names in the text (Grady Lewis, Walter V. Schaefer and a third member) to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; states that it supersedes Executive Order No. 9958, dated May 15, 1948; and, as provided by section 10, it bars National Airlines, Inc., or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9996 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the first part of the order's operative text (the enacting words).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9996 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the continuation of the order's operative text after the interleaved page text.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 9996 at 13 FR 5249 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed September 8, 1948; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the September 10, 1948 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3297 to 3806 and 14343 to 14697 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Public Belt Railroad Commission for the City of New Orleans, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen and the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, labor organizations. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Public Belt Railroad Commission for the City of New Orleans or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 9996 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10032 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10032_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10032_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_cf5124cbbf.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated April 11, 1949 and a letter of transmittal to the President dated Washington, D.C., April 11, 1949; the board states that the President approved, on February 19, 1949, an extension permitting it to file its report not later than April 13, 1949. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking April 11, 1949 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on April 11, 1949 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to May 11, 1949 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President approved on February 19, 1949 an extension of the report time to not later than April 13, 1949; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

Creating an E mergency B oard to I nves­

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Akron, Canton ty  Youngstown Rail­
road Company and certain other carriers 
designated in the list attached hereto 
and made a part hereof, and certain of 
their employees represented by the 
Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a 
labor organization; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here-' 
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ement of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially* to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board 
of three members, to be appointed by 
me, to investigate the said dispute. No 
member of the said board shall be pe­
cuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by any of the carriers involved or 
its employees in the conditions out of 
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10032 at 14 FR 429 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed January 28, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the February 1, 1949 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 580 to 2224 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Akron, Canton & Youngstown Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. The list of carriers (Eastern, Western and Southeastern regions) follows the signature block in the held text; it identifies the carriers and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10032 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10032_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10032_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_cf5124cbbf.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated April 11, 1949 and a letter of transmittal to the President dated Washington, D.C., April 11, 1949; the board states that the President approved, on February 19, 1949, an extension permitting it to file its report not later than April 13, 1949. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking April 11, 1949 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on April 11, 1949 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to May 11, 1949 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President approved on February 19, 1949 an extension of the report time to not later than April 13, 1949; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10037 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the first part of the order's operative text (the enacting words).
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any car­
rier. «
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.

The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the continuation of the order's operative text after the interleaved page text.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10037 at 14 FR 679 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed February 14, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the February 16, 1949 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3718 to 4222 and 9086 to 9418 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Denver & Rio Grande Western Railroad Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Switchmen's Union of North America, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Denver & Rio Grande Western Railroad Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10037 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause; the order created a board for one dispute and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown, and section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues on its own force.
