operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10038 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10038_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10038_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_52bfb598d4.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated September 19, 1949; the board states that the President approved extension requests on February 28, 1949 and on July 27, 1949, the second extending its time to September 19, 1949. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking September 19, 1949 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on September 19, 1949 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to October 19, 1949 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10038 at 14 FR 680 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed February 15, 1949; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the February 16, 1949 issue. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10105 at 15 FR 649 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed February 4, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the February 7, 1950 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 609 to 2212 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Denver and Rio Grande Western Railroad Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Denver and Rio Grande Western Railroad Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10105 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10105_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10105_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_ef4fcb872e.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated February 28, 1950. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking February 28, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on February 28, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to March 30, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10150 at 15 FR 5219 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed August 11, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the August 12, 1950 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3872 to 4182 and 11762 to 12623 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Atlantic & East Carolina Railway Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the sixteen cooperating non-operating labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; directs that each carrier involved be given independent consideration and that the labor organizations be permitted to function as a unit before the board; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and, as provided by section 10, it bars any of the carriers involved or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Lists A and B (the carriers and the labor organizations) follow the signature block in the held text; they identify the parties and are not separate commands. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10150 describes creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10150_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10150_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_519666f265.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated September 9, 1950. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking September 9, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on September 9, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to October 9, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 2 of the Civil Service Act 
(22 Stat. 404) and by section 1753 of the 
Revised Statutes of the United States, it 
is hereby ordered as follows:
1. Except as provided by paragraph 2 
hereof, any employee of the Federal Gov­
ernment without competitive status who 
on the date of this order is serving in an 
active-duty status in an office or position 
in the competitive service of the Govern­
ment shall be entitled to and shall ac­
quire a competitive status upon compli­
ance with the following conditions:
(a) The employee shall have served 
continuously in a full-time, active-duty 
status in the competitive service, without 
a break in service of more than sixty cal­
endar days, during the two years im­
mediately prior to the date of this order:  
Provided, that military service shall not 
be regarded as a break in service.
(b) If his employment is evaluated 
under an efficiency rating system, the 
most recent rating of the employee must 
be “Good” or better, and if his employ­
ment is not so evaluated, the head of 
the agency in which he is employed must 
certify to the Civil Service Commission 
that the employee has served with merit 
for six months or longer immediately 
prior to the date of such certification.
(c) The acquisition of competitive 
status by the employee must be recom­
mended by the head of the agency in 
which he is employed within six months 
of the date of this order.
(d) The employee must successfully 
qualify in such suitable noncompetitive 
examination as the Civil Service Com­
mission may prescribe: Provided, That 
only one such noncompetitive examina­
tion shall be given him.
2. This order shall not be applicable to
(a) postmasters; (b) rural carriers in 
those cases with respect to which there 
is an existing register of eligibles for 
filling the position In question or with 
respect to which an examination has 
been announced by the Civil Service 
Commission for filling such position; and
(c) persons not entitled to veteran pref­
erence who are serving in positions 
which are by law or by Executive order 
restricted to preference eligibles.
3. For the purposes of this order, em­
ployees who are on active military duty 
on the date hereof shall be considered as 
being in an active-duty status.
4. The Civil Service Commission shall 
promulgate regulations to effectuate the 
purposes of this order.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10157
E nabling C ertain  E mployees  of the  
F ederal G overnment  T o A cquire  a 
Competitive  S tatus
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 2 of the Civil Service Act 
(22 Stat. 404) and by section 1753 of the 
Revised Statutes of the United States, it 
is hereby ordered as follows:
1. Except as provided by paragraph 2 
hereof, any employee of the Federal Gov­
ernment without competitive status who 
on the date of this order is serving in an 
active-duty status in an office or position 
in the competitive service of the Govern­
ment shall be entitled to and shall ac­
quire a competitive status upon compli­
ance with the following conditions:
(a) The employee shall have served 
continuously in a full-time, active-duty 
status in the competitive service, without 
a break in service of more than sixty cal­
endar days, during the two years im­
mediately prior to the date of this order:  
Provided, that military service shall not 
be regarded as a break in service.
(b) If his employment is evaluated 
under an efficiency rating system, the 
most recent rating of the employee must 
be “Good” or better, and if his employ­
ment is not so evaluated, the head of 
the agency in which he is employed must 
certify to the Civil Service Commission 
that the employee has served with merit 
for six months or longer immediately 
prior to the date of such certification.
(c) The acquisition of competitive 
status by the employee must be recom­
mended by the head of the agency in 
which he is employed within six months 
of the date of this order.
(d) The employee must successfully 
qualify in such suitable noncompetitive 
examination as the Civil Service Com­
mission may prescribe: Provided, That 
only one such noncompetitive examina­
tion shall be given him.
2. This order shall not be applicable to
(a) postmasters; (b) rural carriers in 
those cases with respect to which there 
is an existing register of eligibles for 
filling the position In question or with 
respect to which an examination has 
been announced by the Civil Service 
Commission for filling such position; and
(c) persons not entitled to veteran pref­
erence who are serving in positions 
which are by law or by Executive order 
restricted to preference eligibles.
3. For the purposes of this order, em­
ployees who are on active military duty 
on the date hereof shall be considered as 
being in an active-duty status.
4. The Civil Service Commission shall 
promulgate regulations to effectuate the 
purposes of this order.
H arry S. T ruman

August 28, 1950.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10157 at 15 FR 5834 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed August 28, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the August 30, 1950 issue. The register title is Enabling Certain Employees of the Federal Government To Acquire a Competitive Status.  Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 3563 to 5979 of the held text, from the enacting words through paragraph 4. The dossier lists ten clauses, including entries with duplicate-style names (a-dup2, c-dup2, c-3, c-4) whose offsets lie within paragraphs 2 to 4; the single clause below covers paragraphs 1 to 4 once. Content: paragraph 1 gives any employee without competitive status who on the date of the order is serving in an active-duty status in a competitive-service position a competitive status on meeting four conditions (continuous service for two years, an efficiency rating or certification, agency recommendation within six months, and a noncompetitive examination); paragraph 2 excludes postmasters, certain rural carriers and certain non-preference persons; paragraph 3 treats employees on active military duty as in active-duty status; paragraph 4 directs the Civil Service Commission to issue regulations. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10157 describes authorizing certain Government employees to acquire a competitive civil service status). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Later events, both strike-and-insert amendments under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 and not ends. (1) Executive Order 10217 of February 26, 1951 amends paragraph 1(c) to read that the recommendation must be made to the Civil Service Commission by the head of the agency within six months of the date of the order, with a proviso extending the period, for an employee who left or leaves his civilian position to enter the armed forces, to six months after honorable termination of military service. (2) Executive Order 10288 of September 7, 1951 further amends paragraph 1(a) by adding a proviso on substitute employees in the postal service appointed on or before August 28, 1948, and amends paragraph 1(c) again by adding a proviso that recommendations in the postal-substitute cases, and in cases of agency inadvertence, may be accepted if received by the Commission not later than March 1, 1952. Neither order has effective-date wording, so each took effect on signing. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain no end date or termination clause; the six-month recommendation window, as extended to March 1, 1952, is a condition on acquiring status and is not an end of the order. Executive Order 10535 of June 9, 1954 (held text) authorizes the Civil Service Commission to confer competitive status on persons who met the requirements of this order, "as amended", but were not recommended through administrative error; it recites this order as still in effect and does not revoke or supersede it, so it is context and not an end. The dossier chain names Executive Orders 10217, 10288 and 12553. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10286 at 16 FR 9135 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed September 6, 1951; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the September 8, 1951 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3554 to 4245 and 13568 to 13837 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span was replaced because the dossier's single span begins in unrelated Federal Register text and omits the opening of the enacting clause. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Pullman Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors of America, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; directs that, in performing its functions under the order, the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Pullman Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10286 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10286_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10286_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_f8fecb191c.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has no readable report date: its first three PDF pages have no text layer in the held text, and the pages that have text show only that the board was created on September 6, 1951 (the National Mediation Board index shows the case closed on October 3, 1951, an index entry and not a report date). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C); because no report date can be read, no functionally-spent date is recorded, and the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The PDF page images are not held in the repository, so a page check of the report is the missing source for a report date. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. The packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts (clause drafts excluded) found citations only in this order's own printing, the National Mediation Board report copy and in the printing of Executive Order 10285, Executive Order 10287, on whose Federal Register page this order's heading also appears; none of those texts acts on this order. The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill and the further commands noted in the inventory all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10306 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10306_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10306_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_97b6e5c39e.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated February 14, 1952; the board states that the President, on December 13, 1951, extended its time to January 15, 1952 and later granted a further extension directing it to file its report by February 15, 1952 (the date of the further extension is not stated). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking February 14, 1952 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on February 14, 1952 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to March 15, 1952 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President extended the report time on December 13, 1951 to January 15, 1952; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

WHEREAS disputes exist between the 
Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Com­
pany and certain other carriers desig­
nated in list A attached hereto and made 
a part hereof, carriers under Federal 
management, and certain workers repre­
sented by the seventeen cooperating 
(non-operating) railway labor organiza­
tions designated in list B attached hereto 
and made a part hereof; and 
WHEREAS by Executive Order No. 
10155 of August 25,1950, possession, con-
trol, and operation of the transportation 
systems owned or operated by the said 
carriers, together with the transporta­
tion systems owned or operated by cer­
tain other carriers, were assumed by the 
President, through the Secretary of the 
Army; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not 
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes threaten, in 
the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to 
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service, and also threaten to 
interfere with the operation by the Sec­
retary of the Army of transportation 
systems taken pursuant to the said 
Executive Order No. 10155:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by the Constitu­
tion and the laws of the United States, 
including section 10 of the Railway 
Labor Act, as amended (45 U. S.C. 160), 
and subject to the provisions of that sec­
tion, I  hereby create a board of three 
members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate the said disputes. Nothing in 
this order shall be construed to derogate 
from the authority of the Secretary of 
the Army under the said Executive 
Order No. 10155.
No member of the said Board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any 
organization of railway employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
disputes within thirty days from the date 
of this order. The Board may, to the ex­
tent it deems necessary or desirable, 
make separate and independent findings 
with respect to each of the carriers in­
volved.
In performing its functions under this 
order the Board shall comply with the 
requirements of section 502 of the De­
fense Production Act of 1950, as 
amended.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10306 at 16 FR 11709 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed November 15, 1951; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the November 20, 1951 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 3795 to 6308 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence. Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company and certain other carriers designated in a list A attached to the order, carriers under Federal management, and certain workers represented by the seventeen cooperating (non-operating) railway labor organizations designated in a list B attached to the order, and that the President had assumed possession, control and operation of the carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 of August 25, 1950. Acting under the Constitution and the laws, including section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; states that nothing in the order is to be construed to derogate from the authority of the Secretary of the Army under Executive Order No. 10155 (the order under which the President had assumed possession of these carriers' transportation systems through the Secretary of the Army); it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; permits the board, to the extent it deems necessary or desirable, to make separate and independent findings with respect to each carrier involved; and directs that, in performing its functions under the order, the board comply with the requirements of section 502 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended. It contains no sentence imposing a status-quo standstill on the carriers or employees. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10306 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10306_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10306_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_97b6e5c39e.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated February 14, 1952; the board states that the President, on December 13, 1951, extended its time to January 15, 1952 and later granted a further extension directing it to file its report by February 15, 1952 (the date of the further extension is not stated). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking February 14, 1952 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on February 14, 1952 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to March 15, 1952 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches. Extension of the report deadline: the held National Mediation Board report copy (a held text lead, not an authenticated original, so it cannot be registered as a later-event source in this sheet) states that the President extended the report time on December 13, 1951 to January 15, 1952; the extension moves the report deadline and is not an end, and it is disclosed here and not entered as a later event.

By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by section 2 of the Civil Service Act 
(22 Stat. 403) and section 1753 of the 
Revised Statutes of the United States 
(5 U. S. C. 631) , it is hereby ordered as 
follows:
S ection  1 . Notwithstanding the provi­
sions of section 1  (a) of Executive Order 
No. 10180" of November 13, 1950, and to 
the extent authorized by law, appoint­
ments to positions in the field service of 
the Post Office Department for which 
salary rates are fixed by the act of 
July 6, 1945, 59 Stat. 435, as amended 
and supplemented, shall be made on a 
permanent basis.
Sec . 2. (a) Under such conditions as the 
Civil Service Commission may prescribe, 
and to the extent permitted by law, .em­
ployees serving under indefinite appoint­
ments in the field service of the Post 
Office Department whose salary rates are 
fixed by the said act of July 6, 1945, as 
amended and supplemented (herein­
after referred to as employees), and who 
were appointed by selection in regular 
order from competitive civil-service reg­
isters established subsequent to Febru­
ary 4, 1946, or who normally would have 
been appointed by selection in regular 
order from such registers, shall have 
their appointments converted to proba- 
tional or permanent appointments as 
of the effective date of this order: Pro­
vided, that such employees have served 
continuously (or without a break in serv­
ice of more than ninety days) since 
•they were appointed: Provided further,  
that the number of employees whose 
appointments may be converted under 
this section shall not exceed the number 
of vacancies in the authorized comple­
ment of permanent positions (consist­
ing of regular positions and positions 
within the authorized quota of substi­
tutes) existing on the effective date of 
this order: And provided further,  that 
employees shall be selected for conver­
sion of their appointments in the order
in which they were or would have been 
within reach for appointment from such 
registers. Employees in excess of the 
number required to fill vacancies in the 
authorized complement of permanent 
positions shall have their names entered 
on appropriate competitive registers and 
thereafter shall be eligible for proba- 
tional appointment in accordance with 
civil-service regulations.
(b) Employees who left positions in 
the field service of the Post Office De­
partment to enter the armed forces of 
the United States and are reemployed 
therein after the effective date of this 
order pursuant to application for re­
employment made within ninety days 
after honorable discharge, or after hos­
pitalization continuing after discharge 
for not more than one year, shall have 
their former indefinite appointments 
converted to probational or permanent 
appointments in accordance with this 
section.
S ec. 3 . This order shall become effec­
tive thirty days after the date hereof.

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10376 at 17 FR 6681 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed July 18, 1952; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the July 22, 1952 issue. The register title is Providing for Permanent Appointments in the Field Service of the Post Office Department.  Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 751 to 3651 of the held text, from the enacting words through section 3. The dossier's clause span (offsets 3054 to 3570) covers only paragraph 2(b) of the order, not the whole order. Content: section 1 provides that, notwithstanding section 1(a) of Executive Order No. 10180 of November 13, 1950 and to the extent authorized by law, appointments to field-service positions of the Post Office Department whose salary rates are fixed by the act of July 6, 1945 are to be made on a permanent basis; section 2(a) converts, under conditions the Civil Service Commission prescribes, indefinite appointments of certain such employees to probational or permanent appointments as of the effective date, limited by the number of vacancies in the authorized complement; section 2(b) does the same for employees reemployed after armed-forces service on application within ninety days after honorable discharge (or after hospitalization continuing not more than one year); section 3 makes the order effective thirty days after its date. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10376 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry, extracted separately and matched by position, reads providing for permanent appointments in the field service of the Post Office Department). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Earlier-end check: no fixed end date or termination clause appears in the order; section 3 sets only an effective date (thirty days after July 18, 1952). Executive Order 10180 is cited by this order and is earlier, so it is not a later event. The packet's number search finds no held text citing this order, and the dossier chain names only Executive Order 12553. No held source shows whether the section 2 conversions were completed or whether a statute or regulation displaced section 1 before 1986, so no earlier end is claimed. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10449 at 18 FR 2469 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 24, 1953; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 28, 1953 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3394 to 4127 and 11203 to 11300 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the New York, Chicago & St. Louis Railroad Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10449 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board record (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10449_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10449_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_890e74e86f.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a National Mediation Board record for Emergency Board No. 104 stating that no members were appointed and that the parties reached agreement on April 26, 1953, so that no emergency board was set up for hearing the dispute; there is no report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on EO 10449 (a board never constituted is treated like the other emergency-board orders) the order stayed on the books until its express revocation; the fact that the board was never constituted is disclosed here, and the agreement of the parties on April 26, 1953 (a statement in that record) is a spent fact and not an end. The thirty-day report deadline (to May 24, 1953 on the inclusive reading) is a deadline and not an end. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. tigate a Dispute Between the Pull­
man Company and Certain op Its

WHEREAS a dispute exists between
The Pullman Company, a carrier, and
certain of its employees represented by
the Order of Railway Conductors and
Brakemen, a labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as

ment of the National Mediation Board,

terstate commerce to a degree such as

essential transportation service:

U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of
three members, to be appointed by me,
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily
or otherwise interested in any organiza­

the President with respect to the said

The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10643_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10643_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_84f930ce02.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated December 12, 1955; the board states that, upon stipulation of the parties, the President extended the time for filing the report to December 12, 1955. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking December 12, 1955 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on December 12, 1955 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to January 11, 1956 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence.

WHEREAS these disputes, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threaten substantially to interrupt inter­
state commerce to a degree such as to*  
deprive the country of essential trans­
portation service;
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of

U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of

to investigate the said disputes. No  
member of the said board shall be pecu­
niarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of employees or any carrier.

the President with respect to the said
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order. *

way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days'after the board

changé, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Albany Port District Rail­
road and other carriers represented by  
the Eastern, Western and Southeastern  
Carriers’ •  Conference Committees or  
their employees in the conditions out of  
which the said dispute arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10643 at 20 FR 8359 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed November 7, 1955; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the November 9, 1955 issue. Inventory: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 638 to 3187 of the held text, from the order's heading through its last operative sentence (the sentence barring changes in conditions). Text: The order recites that disputes exist between the Albany Port District Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees, designated in lists A and C attached to the order, and certain of their employees represented by the cooperating (non-operating) railway labor organizations designated in lists B and D attached to the order, on wage demands and on demands for changes in health and welfare agreements. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the disputes; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Albany Port District Railroad and other carriers represented by the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers' Conference Committees or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the disputes arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10643 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10643_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10643_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_84f930ce02.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated December 12, 1955; the board states that, upon stipulation of the parties, the President extended the time for filing the report to December 12, 1955. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking December 12, 1955 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on December 12, 1955 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to January 11, 1956 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10689 at 21 FR 9161 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed November 22, 1956; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the November 24, 1956 issue. The register title is Creating a Board of Inquiry To Report on Certain Labor Disputes Affecting the Maritime Industry of the United States.  Inventory corrected: one clause, offsets 2453 to 3197 of the held text, from the enacting words through the continuation sentence. The dossier's second span (offsets 3539 to 7169) and third span (7171 to 7900) hold Agricultural Marketing Service regulation text that follows the order in the text layer. Content: a recital of a labor dispute in the maritime industry; under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 the order creates a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues, gives the Board the powers and duties of Title II of the Act, directs a report to the President under section 206 by a stated date, and continues the Board in existence after its report to perform other functions required under the Act until the President terminates it. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10689 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry, extracted separately and matched by position, reads creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report date is a deadline and not an end (owner ruling of 2026-10-21, report deadline). The order says the Board continues after its report until the President terminates it; no held source shows a presidential termination of this Board and no board report is held, so no functionally-spent date is recorded and the revocation is the first end shown. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a continuation until presidential termination, neither of which is an end shown in a held source; the packet's number search finds no held text citing this order; the dossier chain names only Executive Order 12553. Prior research: the dossier shows no canonical prior claim and no conflicting versions. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning.

The order's commands were one-time (creating the Board and its report); no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the subject entry matches, and the enacting sentence has no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order."}

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10696 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). The report deadline and the standstill are not ends. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the first part of the order's operative text (the enacting words).

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10696 at 22 FR 531 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed January 25, 1957; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the January 29, 1957 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3649 to 4017 and 11659 to 12131 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Railway Express Agency, Incorporated, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters, Chauffeurs, Warehousemen and Helpers of America, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Railway Express Agency, Incorporated, or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10696 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). No board report is held for this order (the staged lookup has no National Mediation Board report text for it), so the date the board reported, and whether it did, is not established and no functionally-spent date is recorded; the thirty-day report deadline and the standstill are deadlines and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C). Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a thirty-day report deadline and a standstill running until thirty days after the report, neither of which is an end; no stated fixed end date or termination clause appears in the held text. No other held order text cites this order by number (the packet's bounded number search of 33,118 held texts, excluding clause drafts, found none). The dossier's chain of later events names only Executive Order 12553 as acting on this order, and the three selected machine searches show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the report deadline, the standstill all concern the single dispute the order addressed; none is a separate delegation, standing rule or continuing regulation. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, which continues on its own statutory force; the period it measures here was set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows it still running.","savings_check":"Savings: Executive Order 12553 contains no saving clause (the enacting sentence is followed only by the table). The order's one-time commands (creating the board, the report, the status quo period) were exhausted by performance or lapse, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently and needs no support from this order, and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown in any held source. State none_after_bounded_search.","scope_check":"Scope: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number, the table entry matches the order's subject, and the enacting sentence carries no exception, so the revocation reaches the whole order and every clause inventoried here."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12553 revokes the order without a saving clause; the order created a board for one dispute and no surviving appointment, transfer or right is shown, and section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues on its own force. The bounded search covered the held text of Executive Order 12553, the order's own text and the OFR catalog disposition notes.

Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10709 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a dock company labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking June 7, 1957 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on June 7, 1957 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to July 7, 1957 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. No earlier end is shown in held evidence. This is the first part of the order's operative text (the enacting words).

Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10709 at 22 FR 3309 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed May 9, 1957; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the May 11, 1957 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 3442 to 3599 and 11071 to 11840 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Toledo, Lorain & Fairport Dock Company, the Toledo Lakefront Dock Company and the Cleveland Stevedore Company, carriers, and certain of their employees represented by District 50, United Mine Workers of America, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the three dock companies or their employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10709 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate a dock company labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10811 at 24 FR 3179 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 22, 1959; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 24, 1959 issue. Inventory corrected: two clauses, offsets 4297 to 4413 and 13450 to 14152 of the held text. The text layer interleaves the order with unrelated Federal Register page text (a contents list) between its first and second parts, so the order's operative text is the first part (the enacting words) and the continuation, which are contiguous in the printed order. The dossier's span includes the interleaved unrelated page text. The order's heading and recitals precede the first part and contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Pan American World Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, Air Transport Division, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars Pan American World Airways, Inc., or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10811 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) reads as creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10811_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10811_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_baa6c6b760.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated June 15, 1959 and a letter of transmittal dated Washington, D.C., June 12, 1959; the board states that the parties agreed to extend the time for the report to June 15, 1959. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking June 15, 1959 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on June 15, 1959 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to July 15, 1959 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10842 at 24 FR 8249 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed October 6, 1959; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the October 10, 1959 issue. The register title is Creating a Board of Inquiry To Report on Certain Labor Disputes Affecting the Maritime Industry.  Inventory confirmed: one whole-order clause, the dossier span at offsets 1231 to 2827 of the held text, which runs from the recitals through the continuation sentence and the signing block. The text layer of this page is partly garbled, so no order text is quoted here beyond Executive Order 12553. Content: a recital of a labor dispute in the maritime industry; under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 the order creates a Board of Inquiry to inquire into the issues, gives the Board the powers and duties of Title II of the Act, directs a report to the President under section 206 by a stated date, and continues the Board in existence after its report to perform other functions required under the Act until the President terminates it. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the number 10842 appears in the table's number column, and the aligned subject entry, extracted separately and matched by position, reads creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the maritime industry). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). The report date is a deadline and not an end (owner ruling of 2026-10-21, report deadline). The order says the Board continues after its report until the President terminates it; no held source shows a presidential termination of this Board and no board report is held, so no functionally-spent date is recorded and the revocation is the first end shown. Earlier-end check: the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a continuation until presidential termination, neither of which is an end shown in a held source; the packet's number search finds no held text citing this order; the dossier chain names only Executive Order 12553. § 341.2 Supervisory assistance.
Borrowers will receive supervisory as­
sistance and assistance in developing 
long-time and annual farm and home 
plans, keeping records, and analyzing

extent deemed necessary by the Farm­

§ 341.3 Relationship with production  
emergency loans.
Initial operating loans will not be 
made to applicants in areas designated 
for production emergency loans when 
the credit needed is primarily for an­
nual operating expenses and can be 
scheduled for payment in full from the 
first year’ s operations, provided such ap­
plicant’ s credit needs can be met ade­
quately with such emergency loans.
§ 341.4 Eligibility*
(a) Applicant  To be eligible for a 
loan, the applicant must be an individual 
who:
(1) Is a citizen of the United States.
(2) Possesses legal capacity to con­
tract for the loan.
(3) Is unable to obtain sufficient credit 
to finance his actual needs at rates 
(but not exceeding the rate of 5 per­
cent per annum) and terms prevailing in 
or near his community for loans of sim­
ilar size and character. Real estate 
equity should be considered along with 
the other resources of an applicant in 
determining the availability of credit 
from private and cooperative sources.
(4) Can meet, during the period that 
operating loans likely will be needed, his 
major needs for operating credit within 
the indebtedness limitation prescribed in 
§  341.8, except for the financing of spe­
cial enterprises such as some livestock 
feeding operations, and sugar beets 
where financing on a contractual or 
equally definite basis is available.
(5) Possesses the character, ability, 
industry, and experience necessary to 
carry out successfully the proposed farm­
ing operations and will honestly en­
deavor to carry out the undertakings
and obligations required of him in con­
nection with the loan.
(6) At the time he applies for a loan, 
is the owner-operator of a farm, a farm 
tenant, a farm laborer, a sharecropper, 
or other individual who obtains the 
major portion of his income from farm­
ing. Exceptions may be made to this 
requirement in justifiable circumstances 
for individuals whose normal means of 
livelihood in the past has been farming 
but who may not have depended pri­
marily on farming ^for their livelihood 
during the past few years but not beyond 
five years.
(7) After the loan is made, will be the 
operator of a family-type farm as defined 
in §  341.4(b) as an owner or tenant. 
Such an operator will be considered as 
a full-time family-type farmer. How­
ever, an applicant who will not operate a 
family-type farm as defined in §  341.4(b) 
or who plans to devote a substantial part 
of his time to off-farm employment will 
be considered as a part-time farm op­
erator and will be considered for operat­
ing loans only under the provisions of 
Subpart B of this part.
(b) Family-type farm.  A family-type 
farm is defined as a farm (1) that is of 
sufficient size and productivity to fur­
nish income that will enable a farm 
family to have a reasonable standard of 
living, pay operating expenses including 
maintenance of necessary livestock, farm 
and home equipment, and land and 
buildings, pay their debts, and have a 
reasonable reserve to meet unforeseen 
emergencies, (2) for which the manage­
ment is furnished by the operator and 
his immediate family, and (3) for which 
the labor is furnished primarily by such 
operator and family except during sea­
sonal peak-load periods. It is not in­
tended to include in this definition farms 
which require large amounts of seasonal 
hired labor.
§ 341.5 Certification by applicant.
Before an application for an operating 
loan is considered, the applicant must 
certify in writing on Form FHA-49, “Cer­
tifications—Operating Loans,” that he is 
a citizen of the United States and that 
sufficient credit to meet his actual needs 
for the designated crop year is not avail­
able to'him  at rates (but not exceeding 
the rate of five percent per annum) and 
terms for loans of similar size and char­
acter prevailing in or near the com­
munity where he resides. The applicant 
also must agree to abide by the other 
provisions set forth in P art I of Form 
FHA-49.
§ 341.6 Certification by County Com­
mittee.
Before an operating loan is approved, 
the County Committee must certify in
